member: Dalia - Cooperative Use and Produce Preservation Specialist
message:
Amara, Baraka and Chidi, three-day staged loading fits hand work and keeps first cooling inside solar supply, with harvest in daily lots not one tonne, about 333 kilogrammes per day meaning 17 crates at 20 kilogrammes per crate, kilogrammes means mass, using 600 by 400 millimetre footprint, millimetre means length, in the stacking crate (E36), totalling 50 crates for 1000 kilogrammes in the chamber simulation (E44), and 20 kilogrammes is luggage scale under the 23 kilogramme limit in the lifting guidance (E49), so daily carrying is cooperative work.

Amara, Baraka and Chidi, rot slows when sorting stays outside and air moves around vented crates with oldest sold first, with damaged items removed before loading and stock turning First-In First-Out means oldest sold first, following sorting to eliminate defects in the postharvest practices (E46) and high-humidity storage in the handling practices (E19), with crate gaps and fan flow in the cold room sketch (E32), and daily checks stop one bad crate spreading, suits side racks with central aisle.

Amara, Baraka and Chidi, the box stays food safe by washdown with one crate lifted at a time, using vented food-grade crates in the crate evidence (E52) draining through the floor drain in the cold room sketch (E32), while floor pressure of 2.04 kilopascals, kilopascals means load per area, in the floor pressure calculation (E43) is about a tenth of a person standing, so spreaders carry the tonne. I am not ready, rack guard height and door operation with Chidi remain to fix.
